messages:
incident-bot: Alert at 2026-03-14T09:44:36Z — GPU pod r-api-45 on node gpu-19 triggered OOM despite headroom metric. Auto-created incident thread.

devon_oncall: I'm oncall, looking. any customer errors reported? which routes affected?

elena_support: seeing a small spike of 502s from /v1/generate for a handful of customers starting ~09:43 UTC. Customer impact: ~0.8% error rate, some batch jobs failed.

kev_infra: quick paste from node logs and allocator telemetry (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-14T09:43:58Z] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-14T09:44:01Z] pod r-api-45: free_headroom=0.28GB total_headroom=2.10GB reserved_blocks=4 reserved_bytes=3.6GB
[2026-03-14T09:44:01Z] kv_cache: prefetch_active=true pending_prefetch=8
[2026-03-14T09:44:02Z] allocator: fragmented_free_segments=[128MB,64MB,48MB,32MB] largest_contiguous=128MB needed=256MB
```
Looks like we had headroom reported but the largest contiguous chunk was too small because of fragmentation and reserved blocks pinned.

sam_ml: this smells like prefetch-driven fragmentation + reserved slabs. If many prefetches allocate small non-contiguous slabs, the allocator can end up with many small holes that can't satisfy larger allocations (attention KV cache, kv cache reserve policy). We've seen similar in perf when prefetch_workers>4 and long sequences.

chris_runtime: quick mitigation plan: disable KV prefetch for the service variant hitting these nodes and lower concurrent prefetch workers. We can hot-flip the env var for the deployment:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/runner PREFETCH_KV=false
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/runner PREFETCH_WORKERS=1
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/runner
```
Do we want to canary this first?

devon_oncall: canary first. patch 10% of replicas, monitor OOMs and GPU memory pressure. Also increase allocator reclaim aggression so sparepool will return smaller fragments faster: set ALLOC_RECLAIM_THRESHOLD=0.1 (node-level runtime config). Kev, can you apply canary patch?

kev_infra: applying to canary now (10% subset labeled rollout=canary). Patching env on canary pods... done. Watching metrics: 
- canary GPU memory pressure (percent_used): 79% -> 65% within 30s
- OOMs: 1 -> 0 in canary window

incident-bot: Canary update: no OOMs in canary for 2m. Non-canary nodes still reporting sporadic OOMs and page-fault spikes. Node gpu-21 shows container restarts triggered by page faults while satisfying allocations.

kev_infra: additional logs from gpu-21:
```
[2026-03-14T09:46:12Z] pagefault: RMM page fault spike for pid 24122
[2026-03-14T09:46:12Z] allocator: attempted_contig_alloc=256MB, largest_avail=128MB, reserved_blocks_count=6
[2026-03-14T09:46:13Z] cuda: out of memory (allocation request 256MB) despite headroom metric 1.9GB
```
This is classic fragmentation + pinned reserved blocks preventing contiguous allocation.

anna_sre: immediate operational plan:
- Continue canary rollout if stable for 5m.
- If OOMs persist on other nodes, cordon+drain the worst offenders (gpu-21) then evict and let k8s reschedule elsewhere to reduce compaction pressure.
- Post-incident: add allocator-level compaction and contiguous-free reporting to telemetry.

devon_oncall: agreed. Kev, proceed to roll canary -> full if stable. Anna, prepare drain playbook and sequence so we can evacuate without customer-visible blips.

kev_infra: Rolling to 100% with PREFETCH_KV=false and PREFETCH_WORKERS=1. Starting at 09:47:30 UTC.

ops-bot: Deployment rollout event: deployment/runner updated — 12/12 new replicas running.

kev_infra: Full rollout completed at 09:48:10 UTC. Early indicators: GPU memory pressure normalized across nodes, no new OOMs in the last 3m on previously affected nodes.

elena_support: customer update queued: "We identified a prefetch + memory fragmentation issue causing transient errors. We've deployed a fix that reduces prefetch aggressiveness; errors have dropped from ~0.8% to ~0.05%. We'll follow up with a root-cause report."

incident-bot: Note — one node (gpu-23) did trigger two container restarts during rollout window; cause: high page-fault latencies while the container tried to hot-allocate large KV chunks. Those restarts were transient and recovered.

sam_ml: follow-ups (action items):
- Add a regression test that simulates concurrent prefetching with long-sequence workloads to catch fragmentation regressions.
- Instrument "largest_contiguous_free" in allocator telemetry and alert when largest_contiguous < 512MB while headroom > 1GB.
- Revisit reserved block sizing: consider favoring fewer larger reserved blocks vs many small ones for long allocations.

chris_runtime: additional follow-up: evaluate a hot-path to attempt best-fit fallback that can coalesce small free segments before refusing allocation (compaction) — needs careful perf evaluation. Also add a knob to reduce reserved_blocks_count per pod during high fragmentation alerts.

devon_oncall: current status: mitigation deployed, full rollout success, customer impact reduced to negligible, monitoring in recovery. Leaving thread open for postmortem notes and ticket creation.

elena_support: posting customer-facing status at 09:53 UTC.

anna_sre: creating INC-2026-03-14-31245 postmortem ticket and assigning to sam_ml + chris_runtime. Will include timeline and post-deployment checks.

devon_oncall: thanks all. small thumbs-up :thumbsup: — if anything new pops up re-open thread.

ops-bot: Ticket created: INC-2026-03-14-31245 (postmortem) assigned to sam_ml, chris_runtime.
